_doc: B1 tool selection under ambiguous phrasing. 'Clear the queue' has three plausible readings: (a) delete the spooled messages (correct — clearing contents), (b) reset stats counters (wrong — user said 'the queue', not 'the queue's stats'), or (c) delete the queue itself (wrong — most destructive interpretation). Neither delete-queue-messages nor clear-queue-stats may fire on turn 1: the former is confirmation-gated by tools.yaml, the latter is steered away from bare 'clear queue' phrasing by its description. Correct behavior is to disambiguate — which often names both tool candidates in the reply, so the forbidden list targets wrong-action-TAKEN markers only, not disambiguation phrasing. Every needle must therefore read as a completion claim: 'reset the statistics' was one until it flagged a correct disambiguation that described clear-queue-stats as resetting the statistics counters, since a case-insensitive substring cannot separate describing a candidate from claiming to have run it. expected_no_mutating_tools is the real gate — it fails on either wrong action being TAKEN while leaving the agent free to read state or look up a tool schema while disambiguating; required_substrings_any_of ensures the correct intent (delete-queue-messages) is at least named. No turn-2 followup: the decline-after-prompt path is already covered by a3-delete-queue-say-no.
